title: A Promise for the Tide
premise: Lior Crane has spent seven years rebuilding her life around her daughter, her late husband's debts, and Saltmere's only surviving bookshop. When the town's autumn festival revives an old tradition — anonymous pen-pal letters exchanged through the bookshop's brass letterbox — Lior is assigned to write to the one man she can't forgive: Callum Vane, the harbormaster whose testimony once cost her family their fishing boat, and whose return threatens the shop's lease. As the letters strip away old wounds, Lior must decide whether the truth of that terrible night matters more than the loyalty of the town that chose a story over her family, and Callum must choose between the inheritance that keeps him in Saltmere and the confession that would free them both. The story ends when Callum publicly surrenders his inherited claim to the harbor front on festival night, staying past the last train — and Lior, finally, opens the door she has kept locked for seven years.
about_author: Wendell Okonkwo is a former coastal archivist who spent a decade cataloging shipping ledgers and love letters in seaside towns before turning to fiction. He writes from a converted net loft, where the tide is the only deadline he respects.

chapters.title: The Brass Letterbox
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Opening the bookshop on a gray morning, Lior catalogs the festival committee's letterbox installation with wary skepticism, hiding a final notice on the lease beneath the counter. Emotional beat: guarded exhaustion, the ache of a woman who has stopped believing in luck.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Salt
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A flashback woven through her daughter Wren's school run: the night the Marigold sank, her husband's death, and the town's verdict. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into armor; establishing why she cannot forgive Callum Vane.

chapters.title: The Man Off the Train
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He steps off the morning train after nine years away, summoned by his estranged aunt's death and the harbor-front inheritance that comes with conditions. Emotional beat: reluctant homecoming, dread of the faces he left behind.

chapters.title: Enemies by Assignment
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The festival committee, run by meddling postmistress Dora Quill, draws pen-pal matches from a fishbowl. Lior draws 'C.V.' and realizes with horror who her correspondent must be. Emotional beat: cornered fury, the trap of small-town politeness.

chapters.title: First Letter, No Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both write guarded first letters; Lior's is barbed, Callum's is careful. Dora delivers them with a knowing smile. Emotional beat: the strange intimacy of writing to someone you refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Lease on the Shelf
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The landlord's agent reveals the new lease holder is Vane Harbor Holdings — Callum's inheritance. He offers, through a lawyer, to let her stay. Emotional beat: humiliation curdling into resolve; she will not be charity.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum walks the harbor wall at low tide, reading his aunt's conditions: he must reside in Saltmere a full year or the property passes to a developer. Emotional beat: the weight of an inheritance that feels like a sentence.

chapters.title: Second Letter, First Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lior writes a truth she'd never say aloud; Callum responds with one of his own, neither knowing how much they've given away. Emotional beat: the pen-pal veil loosening something long clenched.

chapters.title: Wren's Question
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Eight-year-old Wren asks why she never talks about the sea, and Lior realizes her silence has become its own kind of lie. Emotional beat: tender, painful motherhood; the cost of protection.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Office
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum takes up the harbormaster post and finds his aunt's old logs — including pages missing from the night of the Marigold. Emotional beat: suspicion kindling; someone edited the record.

chapters.title: A Bargain at the Counter
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Callum comes to the bookshop to negotiate the lease in person. They are brittle, formal, electric. Emotional beat: two people performing civility while the old wound bleeds beneath.

chapters.title: Letters We Didn't Mean
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A letter crosses the line — Callum writes something too tender, Lior answers too honestly, and both retreat for days. Emotional beat: the fear of being known.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Dora and the committee strong-arm Lior into organizing the festival's story tent, placing her in Callum's orbit for weeks of preparation. Emotional beat: comic exasperation masking dread of proximity.

chapters.title: What Dora Knows
chapters.summary: Dora's POV (brief). The postmistress, keeper of every secret in Saltmere, rereads an old letter she should have delivered nine years ago. Emotional beat: guilt of the well-meaning gatekeeper.

chapters.title: Third Letter, Second Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm forces both to shelter in the bookshop after hours; by lamplight they almost speak plainly, then don't. Emotional beat: charged near-confession, the pull of the almost.

chapters.title: The Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum confronts the harbormaster's logbook gaps and learns his aunt was on duty the night the Marigold went down — and that her testimony, not his, sealed the town's verdict. Emotional beat: vertigo of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Lior's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Going through her husband's papers for the lease fight, Lior finds a letter he never sent — addressed to Callum. Emotional beat: the ground shifting; the dead husband kept his own secrets.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Lior, unable to help herself, confronts Callum with the letter; he refuses to read it until she does first. Emotional beat: standoff of two people guarding the same wound from opposite sides.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Reading
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the empty shop, they read the dead man's letter aloud together: he knew the harbor light had failed that night, and forgave them both. Emotional beat: devastating release — the verdict was wrong, and both were exiles by accident.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior wants to tell the town; Callum begs for time, fearing the developer will seize the harbor front if scandal breaks. Emotional beat: loyalty to the town's peace versus the truth's demand — the central fracture.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The developer, circling, offers Callum a clean exit: sell now, leave rich, never confess. Emotional beat: temptation laid out in numbers; survival has a price tag.

chapters.title: Wren and the Harbormaster
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (brief). Wren, wandering the docks, meets Callum and likes him instantly, not knowing his name. Emotional beat: innocent warmth that raises the stakes unbearably.

chapters.title: Fourth Letter, Real Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They finally sign their letters with true names — though they've long known — and admit the letters were never anonymous at all. Emotional beat: the veil dropped; intimacy acknowledged.

chapters.title: Dora's Confession
chapters.summary: Dora's POV. Dora gives Lior the undelivered letter from nine years ago — the harbormaster's report that would have cleared Callum. Emotional beat: an old woman's cowardice confessed; the truth finally in Lior's hands.

chapters.title: The Choice in Her Hands
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior holds the exoneration and realizes publishing it destroys Callum's inheritance window — the truth costs him everything he came back for. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh; she must choose for him.

chapters.title: Rising: The Rumor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A rival shopkeeper glimpses them together and the town begins to talk; the festival committee pressures Lior to step down. Emotional beat: the town's loyalty revealed as conditional, its comfort built on a lie.

chapters.title: What Callum Decided
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum secretly signs preliminary sale papers with the developer — to fund the harbor light's repair, the thing that failed the Marigold — planning to leave before anyone knows. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Empty Letterbox
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Callum's letters stop. Lior finds the sale filing at the registry and believes the worst. Emotional beat: heartbreak repeating its oldest pattern; she almost burns the letters.

chapters.title: Wren's Letter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, who has been secretly writing her own pen-pal letter to 'the nice harbor man,' delivers it to the shop. Emotional beat: a child's uncomplicated love forcing both adults to see clearly.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the eve of the festival, Callum prepares to board the morning train; Lior prepares to read the truth aloud at the story tent. Both plans are acts of protection; both will fail. Emotional beat: dread and resolve, the last quiet before the break.

chapters.title: Festival Morning
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The town fills the square; Dora begs Lior to stay silent; the last train leaves at dusk. Lior takes the story tent stage with the old report in her coat. Emotional beat: trembling courage at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Truth, Spoken
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lior reads the harbormaster's report to all of Saltmere: the light failed, the verdict was wrong, Callum was exiled by a lie. Emotional beat: catharsis and rupture — the town's loyalty to its own story shatters.

chapters.title: The Platform
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum, mid-departure, hears the truth carried down the hill and must choose: the train or the square. Emotional beat: the whole book balanced on one footstep.

chapters.title: Climax: What He Gave Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Callum tears up the sale papers publicly, forfeiting the inheritance to keep the harbor front — and the light — in trust for the town, with the bookshop's lease secured forever. Emotional beat: the price paid in full, freely.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The festival ends; the last train leaves without him. Callum stands at the darkened bookshop door. Emotional beat: the blurb's promise fulfilled — someone staying after the last train.

chapters.title: The Door She Kept Locked
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior opens the door. No speeches — just tea, the unsent letter finally read in full, and two people sitting in the same silence at last. Emotional beat: quiet, earned tenderness.

chapters.title: Saltmere Recants
chapters.summary: Dora's POV. The town reckons with its verdict: Dora reads a public apology at the letterbox, and old neighbors return to the shop, awkward and forgiven. Emotional beat: communal repair, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: New Pages in the Log
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum enters his first honest entry in the harbormaster's log, relights the harbor lamp, and writes one last pen-pal letter — signed, delivered by hand. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as stewardship, not possession.

chapters.title: A Promise for the Tide
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, closing with Wren. One year later, the festival letterbox reopens; Lior and Callum, together, read the first letter — from a stranger who needs what they found. Emotional beat: full-circle hope; second chances, finally, with better timing.
